summary: A page can declare what the user has open (useViewContext, registerViewContext); the chat sends it with each new user message as glirastesViewContext. Unchanged apps: nothing changes; while nothing is registered no field is sent.
howTo: Optional. In a React page call useViewContext({ entity: { type: 'order', id: order.id }, label: order.number }) (null withdraws, unmounting too); outside React call registerViewContext('order-page', entry) from glirastes/browser and the returned function on leaving the page (name the view, no record id or personal data: the name shows in development warnings). One entry can hold an entity and a selection (at most 50 ids); unsaved is its own field. The type must be an entity type the request's tools declare (outputEntities / inputEntities; a selection of another type is dropped, the entry stays with its entity), ids exactly as the app has them, facts are kept only with a schema in the handler's viewContext.facts, route only as an explicit path and a hint; state from the URL query belongs in facts. Nothing is read from the URL. Sent by the bundled Vercel transport with every new user message (also the "continue" message after a cut-off answer and a direct / command), read when it is sent (a queued message carries the view of its send time); approval resume, continueTurn and the budget continuation carry none. When sent, the field replaces a glirastesViewContext of bodyExtras. Past 8 entries the first 8 win, and children register before parents. To turn it off: register nothing (or pass null), or set viewContext: false on the server (createAiChatHandler); there is no switch per chat instance. An own transport adds currentViewContext() as glirastesViewContext: { version: 1, current } itself. The runtime container keeps the server side off. Known limit with piiShield: keep personal data out of labels over 60 characters (changelog 0.25.0).
